_schema.description: Per-module dtype overrides keyed by model variant and mesh shape. Modules without an override use the model-wide default dtype (bfloat16). The model variant key is the basename of the model path; mesh shape is the worker grid (rows x cols, e.g. 1x2 / 1x8). Within a model, lookup tries the exact mesh-shape key first, then 'default'. Module keys: shared_mlp, attention, experts, router, lm_head, embedding. Allowed dtype values: bf16, bfp8, fp32. Besides the module keys, a model entry may set 'single_tile_dest_acc' (bool, default true) -- whether the m<=32 projections accumulate in fp32 (single_tile_matmul_ckc). It sits on the model entry, not a mesh entry, because it is model-wide. A mesh-shape entry REPLACES 'default' rather than merging into it, so it must list every module it wants overridden. 'embedding' cannot be bfp8: the embedding weight is stored ROW_MAJOR and BFLOAT8_B requires TILE.

gemma-4-31B-it._comment_single_tile: 31B turns the m<=32 fp32 dest-accumulation OFF, like E2B and unlike 12B. With it on (the default), 31B at 1x8 collapses into a repetition loop partway through a long-context answer: text_demo_v2 long-context-128k stays coherent for ~55 generated tokens and then emits the same 5-token phrase 40 times. Measured on a real WH T3K, 1x8, real weights, classified on the generated text: HiFi3 + fp32 dest-acc DEGENERATES (532 chars, 40x loop), HiFi3 without it is CLEAN over two runs (718 chars), and HiFi2 without it DEGENERATES again -- so this is specifically HiFi3-without-fp32, not a request for less precision. That non-monotonicity matches the #38306 note in single_tile_matmul_ckc: HiFi4 together with fp32 dest-accumulation trips the Wormhole bug and produces garbage decode, and 31B's shapes reach it one fidelity step lower. Costs nothing: batch-1 decode 52.08 vs 52.09 ms/token (2 reps each), and the 31B full_model gates pass unchanged at pcc 0.9974-0.9986 with argmax identical to HF. Does NOT fix 256k, which still loops; main cannot allocate 256k at all.

gemma-4-E2B-it._comment_single_tile: No dtype overrides -- E2B runs all-bfp8 on the code default. The one entry here turns the m<=32 fp32 dest-accumulation OFF, which is the opposite of every other variant. Measured on a real WH T3K, real weights: test_full_model at 1x1 is 0.9964 without it and 0.9875 with it, and test_attention_paged_decode_via_harness[full-1x1] is 0.9885 without and 0.9814 with (against a 0.986 gate pinned at its own measured value). 12B wants the opposite on the SAME all-bfp8 weights -- 1x8 full_model 0.9736 with, 0.8476 without -- so the weight dtype cannot decide this and it is set per model. Raised fidelity (HiFi3) is kept either way; only the accumulator is dropped.

gemma-4-12B-it._comment_wh_bf16: Measured on a real WH T3K; the figures live in the commit that set each entry. single_tile_matmul_ckc raises the m<=32 projections to HiFi3 + fp32 dest-acc for every weight dtype, so these overrides stack on top of that rather than enabling it. Per-module contribution at 1x8, re-walked on a real WH T3K against test_full_model / test_full_model_decode (gates 0.98 / 0.99): shared_mlp is the one that carries it. bfp8/bf16/bfp8 measures 0.97359 / 0.97825 and FAILS both; promoting shared_mlp to bf16 gives 0.99769 / 0.99288 and PASSES both. lm_head really is noise -- promoting it instead measures 0.97362 / 0.97828 (+3e-5), and all-bf16 adds nothing over shared_mlp+attention (0.99771 / 0.99290) -- so lm_head stays bfp8, which matters because it is the 262144-vocab projection and the largest single weight read per decode step. An earlier decomposition recorded the opposite (shared_mlp 'not needed once attention is bf16', costing 0.0008) and shipped attention-only; that understated the cost by ~30x. 1x8 therefore takes shared_mlp + attention. 1x2 has only 2x12 GB and cannot also take attention in bf16 (it does not allocate), so it takes shared_mlp + lm_head. 1x4 stays all-bfp8 and still gains from the accumulator alone. 'embedding' can never be bfp8 -- it is stored ROW_MAJOR and BFLOAT8_B requires TILE.
